queue_items.claim: The span's bytes are one syntactically continuous sentence rather than atomic sayings cohering, so proverb_cluster mis-types the unit the row itself describes.
queue_items.grounds: Byte tier, every run spliced from the staged verse map: 6:12 carries the run's only nominal subject, אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן , and its first participial predicate, ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה ; 6:13 is entirely dependent - קֹרֵ֣ץ בְּ֭עֵינָו מֹלֵ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֑ו מֹ֝רֶ֗ה בְּאֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו - three participial forms with prepositional phrases, carrying no subject noun and no prefix- or suffix-conjugation verb of its own, and 6:14 continues under the same third-person masculine singular reference, תַּֽהְפֻּכ֨וֹת בְּלִבּ֗וֹ , before the apodosis opens at 6:15 with עַל כֵּ֗ן . The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so the form reading is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings: WEB renders 6:13 as bare relative clauses depending on 6:12, “who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers,” (web:Prov.6.13). A proverb_cluster row claims that atomic sayings cohere as one unit; these member verses are not separable sayings, since 6:13 cannot stand as a saying at all, and the row's own rationale describes the span as one cumulative portrait resolved by a causal clause. The collection's ruled precedent types a syntactically continuous single sentence spanning verses as one proverb-unit regardless of verse count, which is the byte situation here. The span itself is not in question: the causal opener at 6:15 ties the apodosis back to 6:12, a petuchah closes oshb:Prov.6.15 in WLC (tier-3, single-witness, inventory-confirmed), and 6:16 opens the numerical formula.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair, span Prov.6.12-Prov.6.15 unchanged: retype unit_type and literature_type_guess from proverb_cluster to single_proverb under the ruled continuous-sentence precedent (one syntactically continuous sentence spanning verses is one proverb-unit regardless of verse count), and re-open the dependent fields a driver swap re-opens - strongest_rejected_alternative, which must then reject the cluster reading on the dependency bytes of 6:13 rather than on the count of verses, plus confidence, observed_substrate_signals and the device_notes deviation sentence. If the adjudicator instead holds that the three participial clauses of 6:13 are separately quotable sayings, proverb_cluster stands and only the rejection sentence needs its byte ground restated; either way this is a type repair, not a span change.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The span opens with a nominal characterization, "אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן" (oshb:Prov.6.12; “A worthless person, a man of iniquity”, web:Prov.6.12), and continues as a chain of participial clauses sharing that one grammatical subject: a perverse mouth (6.12), winking eyes / signaling feet / motioning fingers (6.13), and a scheming heart (6.14) — a cumulative character portrait rather than direct address or imperative instruction. The chain closes when "עַל כֵּ֗ן" (oshb:Prov.6.15; “therefore”, web:Prov.6.15) draws the causal consequence (sudden, remedyless calamity) from the accumulated portrait, tying 6:15 back to the subject introduced in 6:12 and closing the unit before the numerical formula of 6:16 opens a new list-governed unit.

The repeated hinge-word is not incidental vocabulary here -- it is the word each verse's own point depends on, which is why these two verses read as a matched pair rather than as two unrelated observations that happen to share a term. A second, independently named ground supports the pairing alongside the hinge-word: both verses share the identical appearance-vs-outcome template (what seems/is X in the moment ends in Y), naming the shared structure rather than resting the pairing on the hinge-word alone.
